It is marked no_response, deadline_passed=true, and responded_at is null; therefore the requested merchant proof is unavailable and the workflow should proceed on the evidence available. This status is operationally relevant to adjudication of the refund claim, but is not by itself proof that the refund claim is valid: apply the missing-evidence default only to issues the requested merchant evidence would have addressed.

nodes.text: TXN-C18-PURCHASE has an indirectly linked posted partial refund: TXN-C18-CREDIT for -$180.00 USD on 2026-10-11 08:40Z. Both transactions are tied to ORD-C18 and CRD-C18, and the credit is at MER-C18; no direct REFUNDS edge, reversal, additional same-order transaction, or descriptor is recorded. Against the $240.00 purchase, the graph supports $60.00 remaining unpaid, not non-issuance of all credit.

nodes.label: MemoryNote
nodes.text: When a posted credit matches a purchase through the same order, payment instrument, and merchant, treat it as evidence of a partial credit even without a direct REFUNDS edge; compare amounts and dispute only the residual balance, not the already-credited transaction. Absence of additional records in a searched graph remains a limitation, not proof of non-issuance outside that graph.

nodes.label: MemoryNote
nodes.text: A merchant evidence request marked no_response after its passed deadline establishes that the requested proof is unavailable and that adjudication should proceed on available evidence. It supports a cardholder-favourable missing-evidence treatment only for issues the request could have addressed; non-response alone does not prove the underlying return, receipt, or refund entitlement.

nodes.label: MemoryNote
nodes.text: Order or intake text asserting that merchandise was returned does not by itself establish physical return or merchant receipt. Require logistics, carrier, warehouse, or merchant-acknowledgment evidence; a posted partial refund is evidence of credit amount, not proof of receipt or full settlement.
